goldens.comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.

The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:22-38 — booking lookup via findFirst({where:{id: bookingId}}) has no ownership/tenant scoping in the query itself, relies entirely on later in-code check (informational defense-in-depth gap, conf 100)

adjudication.rationale: The new addGuestsHandler fetches a booking solely by `id` (`prisma.booking.findFirst({ where: { id: bookingId }, include: ... })`) before performing any authorization checks. Authorization is enforced only afterward via `isTeamAdminOrOwner`, `isOrganizer`, or `isAttendee`. This is a verifiable defense-in-depth gap: (1) the query loads full booking-related data (attendees, eventType, references, user credentials/destination calendars) prior to access control, and (2) the handler returns distinct errors (`NOT_FOUND` if missing vs `FORBIDDEN` if unauthorized), allowing booking-ID existence enumeration. The finding accurately describes this condition in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:60-63 — no cap on guests array length, no rate limiting; endpoint can be abused to spam arbitrary third-party emails with calendar invites (P2, conf 100)

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuests` mutation accepts `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.max()`/length cap (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts) and the handler directly uses the array to `createMany` attendees and then calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts). There is no throttling/rate limiting logic in the router or handler. An authorized caller (organizer, attendee, or team admin/owner per the permission check) can therefore submit a very large list of arbitrary emails and trigger outbound email/ICS sends to many third parties, which is a concrete abuse/spam vector introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:104-118 — DB write (createMany attendees) commits before calendar sync via eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees; if sync throws, DB and calendar state diverge with no rollback/compensation (P1, conf 80)

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the code updates the booking in the DB first via prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...) and only afterwards calls eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking). There is no surrounding DB transaction and updateCalendarAttendees is not wrapped in a try/catch, so if the calendar sync throws, the mutation will fail after the DB write has already committed, leaving attendees persisted in the DB while the external calendar update did not occur (no rollback/compensation in the diff).

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:167-171 — email send failures swallowed via `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")`, discarding actual err, handler still returns success (P2, conf 90)

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the call to `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is wrapped in a `try/catch` that catches `err` but only does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` without logging/propagating the actual error. The handler then proceeds to `return { message: "Guests added" };` regardless, so email send failures are silently ignored and the client receives success even if notifications failed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:126-138 — getTranslation invoked per-attendee (including pre-existing attendees) inside map, unnecessary N+1-style fan-out on every guest-add call (P3, conf 60)

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts after updating the booking, the code builds attendeesList via `bookingAttendees.attendees.map(async (attendee) => ({ ..., language: { translate: await getTranslation(attendee.locale ?? "en", "common"), ... } }))`. `bookingAttendees.attendees` includes all attendees (pre-existing + newly added) due to `include: { attendees: true }`, so `getTranslation` is invoked once per attendee on every add-guests call. This is a verifiable per-attendee fan-out that is likely unnecessary (many attendees share the same locale) and can be optimized by caching/grouping translations per locale.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts — redundant second `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow` query for organizer despite booking.user already fetched in initial include; if booking.userId is null, queries user id 0 and throws generic Prisma error instead of controlled TRPCError (P3, conf 70)

adjudication.rationale:
In addGuests.handler.ts, the initial prisma.booking.findFirst() includes `user: { include: { destinationCalendar: true, credentials: true } }`, which (with Prisma `include`) returns the full related `user` record, so the later `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } ... })` is an additional, redundant DB query for organizer data that is already available as `booking.user`.

Also, the code uses `booking.userId || 0`. If `booking.userId` is null/undefined, this queries user id 0 and `findFirstOrThrow` will throw a Prisma not-found error (not a TRPCError), resulting in an uncontrolled internal error path rather than a deliberate TRPCError. This behavior is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:36-38 — isTeamAdminOrOwner AND logic makes team-permission path effectively dead code (P1, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the code defines `isTeamAdminOrOwner` as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. The variable name and typical permission intent (“admin or owner”) imply an OR, but the implementation requires the user to be BOTH a team admin and a team owner. As a result, a pure admin (not owner) or a pure owner (not admin) would fail this branch and be denied unless they are also the organizer or an attendee. This is a concrete logic/correctness issue visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — guests array has no `.min(1)`, empty array passes schema then fails downstream with confusing "emails_must_be_unique_valid" error instead of "no guests provided" (P2, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `addGuests.schema.ts`, `guests` is defined as `z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.min(1)`, so an empty array `[]` is valid input at the TRPC boundary. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` becomes `[]` and triggers `if (uniqueGuests.length === 0) throw ... message: "emails_must_be_unique_valid"`, which is misleading for the specific case of “no guests provided” (it conflates empty input with duplicates/blacklisted/already-attending cases). Even if the current UI tends not to send `[]`, the API schema still allows it, so the finding is a real, verifiable correctness/validation issue in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts — no handling for recurring bookings; only the single booking row by bookingId is updated, sibling occurrences not updated (P2, conf 50)

adjudication.rationale: The handler looks up and updates exactly one booking record via `prisma.booking.findFirst({ where: { id: bookingId } ... })` and `prisma.booking.update({ where: { id: bookingId }, data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})`. There is no logic to find or update other bookings/occurrences. However, the finding assumes that a “recurring booking” has multiple sibling booking rows that must also be updated, which is not established in this diff (it could be correct to add guests only to the selected occurrence). The presence of `parseRecurringEvent(...)` is used only for building the email/calendar event payload, not evidence that multiple DB rows should be updated. So the claim that this is a defect is not verifiable from the diff alone and is largely product-behavior speculation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:145 — updateCalendarAttendees result/errors not checked, proceeds to send success emails regardless of calendar sync failure (P2, conf 50)

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the code `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);` is awaited *before* the email sending. If `updateCalendarAttendees` rejects/throws on failure (the typical error signaling for an awaited async call), execution will stop and the subsequent `sendAddGuestsEmails` call will not run. The finding claims it “proceeds to send success emails regardless of calendar sync failure”, but that is not verifiable from the diff; it would only be true if `updateCalendarAttendees` internally swallowed errors or returned a failure result instead of throwing, which is speculative and not shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:21-33 — booking lookup doesn't check booking.status; guests can be added to a CANCELLED or REJECTED booking with no guard (P2, conf 50)
